attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 30 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. Its whole body is two sentences: he was a monk in the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Saint Sergius, in September of the year 1495 he was elected metropolitan of Moscow, and he fell asleep in peace in 1511 and was buried in the church of the Dormition of the Mother of God in the Kremlin. The September 1495 is an election and not a date of life, so it is recorded here and not in `dates`. The monastery of Saint Sergius is a dedication and not a relation, so there are no `related` rows. No year of birth, no kindred and no act of his metropolitanate are printed. The corpus's Maximus of Moscow is another man, and its Stephen of Perm and Stephen of Vladimir, both kept by the same calendar in this same week, are others again. It prints no hymn; the burial place is the only relic notice it gives.
